public import FormalConjecturesUtil
public import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.HardyLittlewood

/-!
# Erdős Problem 855

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)

This is an "eventually" formulation of the Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Nat.Prime

namespace Erdos855

/--
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for all sufficiently large $x, y$, i.e. for all $x, y \ge N$ for some $N$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_855 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᶠ (xy : ℕ × ℕ) in atTop ×ˢ atTop, π (xy.1 + xy.2) ≤ π xy.1 + π xy.2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos855

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the inequality holds “for large x and y”; Lean expresses this using eventuality in the product filter atTop ×ˢ atTop on ℕ × ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Using Filter.prod_atTop_atTop_eq and Filter.eventually_atTop_prod_self', the right-hand side is equivalent to ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ x ≥ N, ∀ y ≥ N, π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y. Thus the threshold is uniform in both variables, exactly as required. Requiring N ≥ 2 or using strict thresholds gives equivalent statements. These equivalences were proved in the scratch file without using any conjecture.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the sole declaration. Nat.primeCounting counts primes up to and including its argument, and the answer slot has the correct scope and polarity. Lean checks confirmed the filter is nontrivial, verified the small boundary cases, and tested the inequality for all integer pairs 2 ≤ x,y ≤ 200. Live requests to erdosproblems.com were Cloudflare-blocked; the cited page was read through its 2026-07-09 archive snapshot (last edited 2026-04-08). That source and the currently accessible independent database both record the problem as open.
